newsitem.title: USA: At Home rockets more than 100 pct after IPO.
newsitem.headline: At Home rockets more than 100 pct after IPO.

text.p: Strong demand for shares of high-speed Internet access company At Home Corp more than doubled the stock's price when it opened for trading on Friday.
The stock, which opened near midday, was up 13-1/4 at 23-3/4. Its IPO price was 10-1/2.

Nine million shares of At Home were sold by the Redwood City, Calif., company. Its service allows customers to hook up their PCs to the Internet over existing cable television coaxial cables via cable modems.
The service is more than 300 times faster than typical dial-up modems, the company said in its prospectus.
At a stock price of $22, the company has a market capitalization of $2.61 billion. It said it would have rougly 118.6 million shares outstanding after the IPO.
The stock was one of the most active issues on the Nasdaq, with over 3.6 million shares changing hands.
Morgan Stanley & Co and Merrill Lynch were co-lead underwriters of the initial public offering.
